newsitem.title: UK: Med/W African markets soft as refiners hold back.
newsitem.headline: Med/W African markets soft as refiners hold back.

text.p: Mediterranean and West African crude oil markets saw limited action on Tuesday as poor refining margins continued to hamper local buying interest and the U.S. market remained subdued, traders said.

Traders took a "wait and see" attitude on news from Nigerian oil ministry sources that workers of Nigeria's Department of Petroleum Resources (DPR), which rubber stamps oil export documents, had threatened to strike from Friday if the backlog of their salaries had not been paid by then.
"We don't know much about it yet so we'll wait for more news," one commented adding that in such a weak market delays would have to be substantial to support prices from slipping further.
Nigerian crudes were under pressure on Tuesday with gas oil rich grades taking the brunt of a poor gas oil/crude crack, traders said.
Forcados barrels were still available in the second decade of March and the grade was assessed by some as low as Dated Brent +40/45 cents though most felt the market up to five cents higher.
"It's hard to say because it hasn't traded for a while. There is a bit of a respite until all the crude, much of which is unsold, arrives in the U.S." one seller said.
Bonny Light held relatively strongly around dated Brent +55/60 cents, while Bonny Medium was under strong downward pressure at dated Brent +30-35 cents.
Cargoes of Qua Iboe were heard offered at dated Brent +55 cents and many expected the next deal to be completed around dated Brent +50 cents.
The Urals port of Novorossiisk was open on Tuesday but one berth was heard unoccupied despite ships waiting at anchor.
Shipping sources said they were unsure of the reason for the delay "but we know it's not the weather."

Two cargoes of Urals may have traded on Tuesday though full details were not available. The cargoes were both prompt with one already on the water and one was heard to have been bought on a quotes related basis.

Traders and refiners alike saw Urals holding around dated Brent -$1 a barrel though lower prices have been heard for distressed cargoes. Sources said that although all February loadings had been sold two weeks ago loading delays due to weather problems meant some buyers had refused the cargoes.
The planned maintenance on the main export pipeline, which should last 3-4 days, has been postponed once again. The maintenance was now expected to be in the first week of March.
